title: Registering a higher-priority hook during emit duplicates an existing handler
normalInput: A real HookRegistry with two async-capable handlers; while emit waits on the first, register a third handler at higher priority. All data is in memory and handler results are ordinary messages.
observed: Existing-high runs twice, existing-low once, new-high zero times in the same emit. Final registration count is 3 and aggregated messages contain the existing-high message twice.
controls: All handlers registered before emit run once each in descending priority
The suspended handler with no mid-emit register runs once
evidenceLevel: actual HookRegistry source + bounded in-memory fake handlers; no Engine or shell runner
missingContract: The public SDK exports HookRegistry, but a supported normal Engine/SDK producer timing and an explicit mid-emit registration visibility/once-per-chain contract were not established. Therefore no product bug severity or Engine duplicate-injection claim.
